title: KV: anchor-based prefetch + lease eviction windows to reduce fragmentation and tail latency
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: under mixed chat + embedding workloads we observed persistent KV cache fragmentation and frequent small-page spillovers that increase memory overhead and 95th percentile latency during bursts. This PR introduces an anchor-based prefetch + lease-based eviction windows strategy and an asynchronous anchor compactor to reduce fragmentation without blocking hot-path serving.

What this change does (single-string description): Implements a lightweight CacheAnchors table that tracks granular page anchors (page start addresses and occupancy metadata), a heatmap-driven prefetcher that favors reads around high-occupancy anchors, and a lease eviction window that soft-pins recently-accessed anchors for a decay period to avoid evicting working sets prematurely. Adds an async anchor compactor that performs low-priority page rewrites to defragment scattered entries and coalesce partially-filled pages back into full pages. The eviction logic now considers anchor age, occupancy ratio, and tenant affinity; it exposes runtime knobs for eviction aggressiveness, anchor decay interval, and compactor backoff. Kernel/runtime interaction: adds a small alignment hint to the kernel path to reduce copy overhead for compactor rewrites, and modifies the batching scheduler to allow cooperative compactor CPU time slices without impacting token-level latency.

Why now: recent customer workloads (tenants with thousands of short-lived sessions) showed >20% memory blowup and repeated spill I/O under queued bursts. This approach reduces tail work by avoiding aggressive per-request evictions and amortizing compaction.

Benchmarks: microbench harness (mixed chat+embedding synthetic trace) shows: 95th latency reduced by ~18% (from 210ms to 172ms) for small seqs under 16-GPU cluster; sustained throughput improved ~12% under steady-state load due to fewer spill IOs; resident KV memory usage reduced ~22% after 30 minutes of steady traffic versus current main. Perf tests attached in PR (perf/artifacts).

Compatibility and rollout: all new behaviors are behind runtime feature flags (kv.anchor_prefetch, kv.lease_evict_windows, kv.anchor_compactor). Defaults are disabled in main; tests enable them. Config can be toggled per-tenant in Dedicated/Private deployments.

Testing: unit tests for CacheAnchors and eviction heuristics added; integration test simulates heavy fragmentation and validates compactor eventually reduces page count and that hot-path latencies stay stable. Added telemetry metrics: kv.anchor_hits, kv.anchor_prefetch_count, kv.compactor_rewrites, kv.eviction_window_evictions.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4821) and reviewed by runtime team
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Benchmarks run in perf lab and artifacts uploaded
- [x] Runtime knobs exposed and documented

Notes: this is intentionally conservative to avoid regressions in multi-tenant scenarios; compactor rate is capped per-node and backs off automatically on IO pressure.
